requirement:
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
rationale:
The subject has three obligations. `Criterion::execute` can compute an answer with no model provider. A criterion can compute its answer directly from tracked inputs. Deterministic execution needs no configured agent. The reviewed tests cover all three.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[deterministic_validation_uses_required_storage_without_an_agent]`
  - It builds a `Memory` graph with no agent. It asserts that `ValidationContext::ask::<bool>` returns `ValidationError::NoAgentConfigured`, so no agent really is configured.
  - `validation::verify` on the same graph still succeeds. The test asserts the computed output: `result` is false and `rationale` is "ordinary computation".
  - It stores the evidence and loads it back. It asserts that `dependencies[0]` is `Dependency::Node(Node(1), fingerprint)` with the fingerprint value "ordinary computation". This shows the answer was computed from a tracked input and the dependency was recorded.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]`
  - The domain has an agent configured with a deliberately broken credential.
  - The deterministic question (`Question(false, …)`) succeeds through `refresh_evidence`. It gives output false and one tracked dependency. So deterministic execution does not touch or require the agent, even a broken one.
  - The question that asks the agent (`Question(true, …)`) fails with `ValidationError::Agent` and names the credential. This contrast shows the success of the deterministic path is not accidental.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[caller_reuses_negative_answers_and_compares_revisions_explicitly]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` give further coverage.
  - Both run purely deterministic criteria through `validation::verify`. Neither is given an agent.
  - They assert typed outputs, the execution and write counts, that `verify` does not persist records, that dependencies are recorded or empty as expected, and that `check_inputs` accepts the stored records.

The inputs tested include dependency-bearing computation (`Node` reads), dependency-free computation, and the no-agent and broken-agent configurations. I found no plausible violation they would accept. Examples are an `execute` that requires an agent, or a deterministic answer that ignores or fails to record tracked inputs. I found no marking gaps, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.
